areas.realistic_ceiling_2026: Repeatable ceiling £1.0m–£1.28m on the prime villa streets (Chantry, Amesbury, St Agnes, Oxford, Wake Green best stretch) — multiple £900k–£1.28m Land Registry sales 2023–26, not one-offs. Area record ~£1.4m (St Agnes Rd 2022). Off the prime grid, well-finished family semis (School Rd/Cambridge Rd/Grove Ave belt) repeatably make £550–900k. This is roughly double the Vicarage Rd £680k record.
areas.ppsqft_finished: Finished/renovated Moseley stock: ~£300–350/sq ft on the good streets — School Rd £351, Greenhill Rd £346, St Mary's Row £346, Cambridge Rd £341, B13 9TS £328, Forest Rd £306, Wake Green Rd £305, Park Rd £303 (housemetric/bricksandlogic). B13 9 sector majority band £215–341/sq ft; tired stock and the Anderton Park/Balsall Heath fringe trade at £180–250/sq ft. Meaningfully above Kings Heath's £280–310 at the top, similar mid-market.
areas.planning_constraints: TWO Article 4(2) conservation areas cover most of the prime streets. (1) Moseley CA (desig. 1983, ext. 1987 & 2005, ~90ha): The Green, Alcester Rd, St Mary's Row, Salisbury Rd, Chantry Rd, Amesbury Rd, Park Hill, Reddings Rd, Woodbridge Rd, Church Rd — Article 4(2) removes PD for highway-facing alterations (windows, porches, re-roofing). (2) St Agnes CA (desig. 1987, ext. 31 Jul 2009, 27.6ha; Art.4(2) in force 31 Jul 2009, confirmed 25 Sep 2009, ALL houses covered): Oxford Rd, St Agnes Rd, Colmore Crescent, Dyott Rd, Yew Tree Rd, plus parts of Wake Green Rd, Billesley Lane, Grove Ave, Cotton Lane, Greenhill Rd and School Rd. Crucially, in ANY conservation area loft dormers (Class B) and side extensions are NOT PD and the 6m/8m larger-home rear scheme doesn't apply — so the panelised PD-extend model only fully works OUTSIDE both CAs: Anderton Park Rd, Leighton Rd, Park Rd/College Rd fringe, School Rd south end towards Kings Heath, Cambridge Rd, Springfield Rd, Thirlmere/Windermere estate roads (verify exact boundary on BCC maps — medium confidence on individual street edges). No Bournville Village Trust scheme in B13 (that's B30/B14 west). Flood: central Moseley is high ground FZ1; the River Cole corridor on the eastern edge (Yardley Wood Rd/Sarehole Mill, B13 0) carries FZ2/3 — avoid Cole-side plots.
areas.project_archetype: The play that works is the PRIME-STREET VILLA REFURB, not the 3-bed extend: buy an unmodernised big period semi/detached on Chantry/Amesbury/St Agnes grid at £750–850k (53 Chantry Rd, £785k Jan 2026, is the template — ~£220–250/sq ft unrefurbished), full sympathetic refurb of ~3,000–3,500 sq ft at £80–100/sq ft (mostly internal, so Article 4 bites little; any rear extension by full application, usually consented behind the building line), exit £1.25–1.35m at ~£350/sq ft. The mid-market version — dated 3-bed semi ~£430–460k on School Rd (outside-CA stretch), add ~45m² rear+loft PD at ~£90–95k — struggles: exit ~£620–640k barely covers cost.
areas.est_net_margin: Villa refurb: buy £785k + SDLT £68.6k (std £29.3k + 5% surcharge £39.3k) + fees £8k + refurb 3,200 sq ft @ £90 = £288k → all-in ~£1.15m; sell £1.28–1.35m (evidenced) → NET ~£130–200k on ~£1.15m deployed. Mid-market extend: buy £430k + SDLT £33k (incl. £21.5k surcharge) + fees £5k + 500 sq ft add @ £190 = £95k + £55k refurb = £618k all-in; sell 1,900 sq ft @ £330 = £627k → NET ~£10k — FAILS; only works if bought at auction ~£350k or self-capped SDLT-free. Auction terrace flip (£190k guide + £85k works, exit ~£420k) nets ~£40–60k.
areas.verdict: Better than the B14 7QG home play, but only at the top end: Moseley's repeatable ceiling (£1.0–1.28m) and finished £/sq ft (£300–350) roughly double Vicarage Road's, giving ~£130–200k net on a prime-street villa refurb vs ~£80–110k at home — however it needs ~2x the capital, the best streets sit under two Article 4 conservation areas that kill the pure PD-extend model, and the ordinary 3-bed extend play actually nets LESS than at home because Moseley entry stock is fully priced.

areas.realistic_ceiling_2026: Repeatable ceiling ~£425–475k for a large finished 4-bed semi on the best streets (Pineapple Rd, Cartland Rd, Hazelwell Lane, Bournville Lane end). The £520k record (2022) and £575k asking are outliers, not repeatable. Terraces — the bulk of the stock — cap at ~£330–350k.
areas.ppsqft_finished: £230–309/sqft (Bricks & Logic street data): Twyning Rd £309, Warren Rd £276–279, Pershore Rd corridor £230–242. Renovated period stock on the best side streets achieves ~£280–310/sqft — no better than mid-market Kings Heath. areas.planning_constraints: No conservation area and no Article 4 direction over Stirchley's terraced grid — full PD rights (rear + loft) intact on Cartland Rd, Pineapple Rd, Hazelwell, Twyning, Warren, Umberslade, Fordhouse Lane east of the Cross-City line. Constraints start at the edges: (1) Bournville Village conservation area + Article 4(2) and the BVT Scheme of Management (deed of covenant, BVT consent for any alteration) apply just west across the railway (Bournville Lane west end / Mary Vale Rd side) — check the BVT boundary map on any border street; (2) River Rea flood warning area (EA zone 033FWF3REA006) specifically covers parts of Cartland Road and Dogpool Lane, 'the Avenues', and low-lying land along Fordhouse Lane — ~200 homes at risk in Bournville/Stirchley; plot-level EA check essential as it hits insurance, lending and resale; (3) Stirchley Framework SPD governs the Pershore Rd commercial corridor, not residential extensions.
areas.project_archetype: Pure refurb, NOT extend-arbitrage: buy a dated 3-bed terrace ~£235k (Cartland Rd type, outside the flood polygon), cosmetic-to-medium refurb plus a modest 15–20m² PD rear infill, sell ~£340–350k against the Brent Rd £332.5k comp. The extend-a-semi version (buy unmodernised at £315k, add ~450 sqft loft+rear to ~1,450 sqft, sell ~£435k) does not clear costs because entry pricing has already gentrified to within ~£110k of finished values.
areas.est_net_margin: Terrace play: exit ~£345k (1,150 sqft x £300) − £235k entry − £14k SDLT (incl. 5% surcharge) − £47.5k build (250 sqft x £190) − £35k refurb − £5k fees ≈ £5–15k net. Semi extend play: £435k exit − £315k entry − £21.5k SDLT − £85.5k build (450 sqft x £190) − £45k refurb − £5k ≈ MINUS £35k. Extend-arbitrage fails; best realistic outcome is low tens of thousands on a keenly-bought terrace.
areas.verdict: Worse than the B14 7QG home play: Stirchley's repeatable ceiling (£425–475k, record £520k) sits far below Kings Heath's, its finished £/sqft (£280–310 best streets) is no higher, and gentrification has already bid unmodernised entry stock to ~£290/sqft, compressing net margins to roughly £0–15k (negative on semis) versus ~£80–110k at home — it remains a pure-refurb or buy-and-hold market, with the only upside being a possible ceiling re-rating around the new Pineapple Road station over 2–3 years.

areas.realistic_ceiling_2026: Repeatable ceiling ~£850,000–£950,000 for a finished 2,400–2,800 sq ft villa on Oakfield Rd / Selly Park Rd / Elmdon Rd / Serpentine Rd, underwritten by QE hospital + University of Birmingham professional/consultant demand. Terrace streets (Kitchener/Cecil/Fashoda) cap out ~£300–320k and are a different, weaker market.
areas.ppsqft_finished: Finished big villas ~£350–£370/sq ft (Selly Park Road modelled at ~£370/sq ft, avg home ~£760k — Varbes); renovated mid-market terraces ~£280–£310/sq ft; dated villa stock trades nearer ~£250–£270/sq ft raw. The ~£100/sq ft dated-to-finished spread, on top of £150–190/sq ft headroom over the client's build cost, is the arbitrage — comfortably above the ~£250 viability floor.
areas.planning_constraints: Two conservation areas, BOTH with Article 4 directions — most of the high-ceiling streets are inside. (1) Selly Park Conservation Area (extended/CAAMP adopted Aug 2022): bounded by Bristol Rd (N), Pershore Rd (E, odd nos. to 643), Selly Park Rd/Woodside Rd (S), Bournbrook Rd (W); includes Elmdon Rd, Selly Wick Rd (boundary runs mid-street to Seymour Close), Selly Wick Drive, Serpentine Rd and the Oakfield Rd frontages. Article 4(2) withdraws PD for any enlargement/alteration, roof-slope change or porch fronting the street; CA status itself also removes PD rear dormers (Class B), side extensions and the 6m larger-home rear extension — so lofts and big rears need full planning (rear, sympathetic schemes are generally consentable, but budget 8–12 weeks and design fees). (2) Selly Park Avenues CA + Article 4: First–Fourth Avenues and Sir Johns Rd east of Pershore Rd. FREE of CA constraint: Upland Rd (south of Selly Park Rd), Warwards Lane, and the Selly Park South grid (Kitchener/Cecil/Hobson/Fashoda/Dogpool Lane) — but that grid IS the River Rea flood corridor (flooded 2008; £4m EA defence scheme completed Mar 2019 protecting 250+ homes; residual insurance/valuation drag). No Bournville Village Trust estate-management scheme applies anywhere in Selly Park (BVT is further SW).
areas.project_archetype: Buy a dated/unmodernised large Victorian semi or detached (~2,000–2,400 sq ft) on Oakfield Rd / Elmdon Rd / Selly Wick Rd / Serpentine Rd / Upland Rd at £500–600k (cf. £600k Oakfield Rd, Mar 2026); full refurb plus ~400 sq ft rear extension (planning application, not PD, inside the CA — Upland Rd keeps PD); finish to ~2,600 sq ft and sell £880–950k to QE/university professional buyers. AVOID the cheap-looking Kitchener/Cecil terrace play: £205–265k entry is tempting but the terrace ceiling (~£310k) and flood-corridor stigma kill the margin after the 5% surcharge.
areas.est_net_margin: Entry £550k → SDLT £45.0k (standard £17.5k + 5% surcharge £27.5k) + £5k fees; add ~400 sq ft at £190/sq ft = £76k; whole-house refurb of existing ~2,200 sq ft at ~£50/sq ft = £110k. Total in ≈ £786k. Exit 2,600 sq ft × £350/sq ft = £910k. Net ≈ £120–125k; range £90–165k across entry £500–600k and exit £340–370/sq ft. Beats the home-street £80–110k, but requires ~£790k capital deployed (roughly double the B14 play) and disciplined entry below ~£575k — at a £650k entry the margin collapses to ~£25k.
areas.verdict: Better than the B14 7QG home play: the ceiling is £850k–£1.15m versus Vicarage Road's £680k hard cap, and finished ~£350–370/sq ft clears the client's £180–200 build cost by ~£160/sq ft (Kings Heath clears only ~£100), giving ~£120–165k net — but it demands nearly twice the capital, sub-£575k entry discipline, and full planning (Article 4 conservation area) instead of PD on the best streets.

Repeatable 2026 ceiling: ~£600–675k on the best Trust streets (Selly Oak Rd, Acacia Rd, Linden Rd area) and ~£650–750k attempted on Middleton Hall Road (off-Trust) — but note MHR's highest VERIFIED sale is only ~£450k, so the £700k+ tier there is asking-price evidence, not yet proven by completions. Realistic finished resale for a renovated family house: ~£280–310/sq ft, with £320+ only on the best streets/product.
areas.planning_constraints: Two overlapping regimes. (1) ON-TRUST (avoid for extend-arbitrage): the Bournville Village Trust Scheme of Management (High Court-approved 1972, amended 1991/2002, under s.19 Leasehold Reform Act 1967) covers the ~1,000-acre estate — the historic core around the Green (Sycamore Rd, Acacia Rd, Laburnum Rd, Willow Rd, Linden Rd, Selly Oak Rd, Woodbrooke Rd, Maple/Beech/Thorn Rds, west Bournville Lane) plus Weoley Hill/Shenley — requiring BVT written consent for any external alteration per its Design Guide zones (street checker on bvt.org.uk), with breach-enforcement powers; the Bournville Village Conservation Area ALSO carries an Article 4(2) Direction removing PD for even minor works (porches, windows, re-roofing). Double-locked: PD effectively dead on Trust land. (2) OFF-TRUST (viable): the Cotteridge/Kings Norton grid east and south of the railway/Pershore Rd — Middleton Hall Rd, Westhill Rd, Midland Rd, Northfield Rd, Cotteridge Rd, Frances Rd, Beaumont Rd, Franklin Rd/Mary Vale Rd Victorian terraces — is outside the BVT scheme, outside any conservation area, no Article 4: full PD rights (Class A rear extensions + loft dormers). Caveat: verify each address against the BVT Scheme of Management map and Design Guide street checker before offering — boundary streets exist. Flood: River Rea corridor (Flood Zones 2/3) clips Stirchley/Cotteridge low ground — Cartland Rd, Dogpool Lane, 'the Avenues', Sir John's Rd areas are in the flood warning zone; Middleton Hall Rd high ground is unaffected.
areas.project_archetype: Off-Trust Cotteridge big-footprint play: buy a dated/unmodernised large Edwardian semi on or off Middleton Hall Road / Westhill Road at ~£400–450k (~2,000–2,200 sq ft), full refurb (~£60/sq ft) plus modest PD rear extension (~30m²/320 sq ft at ~£190/sq ft), sell ~£700–730k towards the street's new asking tier. Budget alternative: 3-bed semi at ~£300k + 45m² rear+loft (~£95k) + £45k refurb, exit ~£520k at ~£300/sq ft. Do NOT buy on Trust land — the premium streets (Selly Oak Rd, Acacia Rd etc.) carry the highest £/sq ft but BVT consent + Article 4 kill the PD extend model.
areas.est_net_margin: Big-semi archetype: exit £730k − entry £425k − SDLT £32.5k (standard £11.25k + 5% surcharge £21.25k) − fees £5k − works £189k (2,200 sq ft refurb @£60 + 320 sq ft added @£190) = ~£78k net. Budget archetype: £520k − £300k − £20k SDLT (£5k + £15k surcharge) − £5k − £140k works = ~£55k net. Range ~£55–90k, and the upper case depends on Middleton Hall Road's £700k+ asking tier actually completing (unproven vs £450k verified record).
areas.verdict: Marginally WORSE than or at best equal to the B14 7QG home play: the true Bournville premium (£300+/sq ft) is locked behind BVT covenants + Article 4 where PD projects are non-viable, while the off-Trust Cotteridge streets where projects ARE viable price at ~£280–310/sq ft finished against £300–450k entry — yielding ~£55–90k net versus the home play's £80–110k — its only real edges being the direct Camp Hill line link from Kings Heath and MHR's untested upside above £700k.
